decisions.mark: states that the strong wording is EARNED PER CALL by querying which corpora the search did not read, rather than being attached to a result shape
explains that a single token matching nothing was previously treated as proof of absence, and that this confuses "nothing exists" with "I did not look there"
states that the downgrades are ORDERED most-specific first, and explains why — a matching row in an unread corpus is a statement about THIS query and outranks statements about the index as a whole
conveys that there is exactly ONE absent-corpus downgrade and that keeping it to one is deliberate, because downgrading on every absent layer turns the grading into a blanket hedge
conveys the general rule the module leaves behind — fix the corpus, not the sentence about the corpus
distinguishes all three grades an empty reply can receive: definitive for the scope, definitive for a reason that is not absence, and not definitive
